title: The First Real Full-Color Printer, 45 Shades From Five Spools & a Printable Robot Vacuum
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: HeyGears G1X: The First Real Full-Color 3D Printer
topics.description: Full-color prints on a desk — and the Kickstarter closes tomorrow

slides.heading: HeyGears G1X: Full Color Comes Home
slides.body: This is the machine everyone's reviewing right now — a desktop printer that jets CMYK ink INTO the model as it builds. Full-color figures, no painting. Steve Makes Everything got hands-on; his macro shots tell the story better than any spec sheet.

slides.heading: What the G1X Actually Is
slides.body: A 3-in-1: full-color 3D printing with UV-cured resin, 3D texture printing, and flat 2D UV printing on wood, metal, acrylic — 400+ materials. The color engine is an industrial Epson i3200 printhead laying 3.9-picoliter droplets of CMYK plus white, clear, and support.
bullets: Full-color 3D on a desk — until now this tech cost as much as a car
8-channel ink system builds color into the model layer by layer — no post-paint
Doubles as a 2D UV flatbed printer: 330 × 420 mm bed, prints on 400+ materials
Reviewers agree the 2D output is superb; 3D sharpness still trails a good resin printer

slides.heading: The Kickstarter Closes TOMORROW — Don't Back It
slides.body: The campaign has raised over $16.5 million from about 3,800 backers and ends September 11. My advice stands: don't buy the Kickstarter. Let the first wave eat the beta pain — this is v1 hardware with unfinished software.
bullets: Roughly $3.3–3.6k on Kickstarter for the full-color 3D config, against a $5.5k MSRP
Reviewers call it 'hugely promising beta hardware' — messy ink handling, gloves required, ~5-minute manual changeover between 2D and 3D modes
Batch print times are still unpublished — the one number a small shop would need
Watch this one mature: the tech is real, the product isn't finished

topics.title: Prusament PLA ColorMix: 45 Shades From Five Spools
topics.description: Prusa open-sources halftoning for filament printers

slides.heading: ColorMix: 45 Shades From Five Spools
slides.body: Prusa's answer to the color question, from the other direction: instead of new hardware, math. Load cyan, yellow, magenta, black, and white — the slicer alternates the colors by layers, and from viewing distance your eye blends them. Halftoning, exactly like an inkjet.
bullets: Five CYMKW spools mix into 45 distinct shades — announced September 8
Works in PrusaSlicer and EasyPrint on ANY multi-color setup: MMU3, XL, INDX
The mixing model is open source — built on the community's Full Spectrum project
Bundle with all seven spools (the five colors plus two glitters) is $209.99; singles $32.99

topics.title: Bambu Is Now #1 — The Numbers Behind the Price War
topics.description: Context's full-year data crowns a new entry-level king

slides.heading: Bambu Overtakes Creality as the #1 Entry-Level Brand
slides.body: Market-research firm Context published its full-year 2025 shipment data: Bambu Lab took 37% of the sub-$2,500 segment and knocked Creality off a top spot it held for years. Remember last week's slide — Creality selling more printers and losing money? Same story, other side.
bullets: Bambu: 37% of entry-level shipments; Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic round out the top four
The whole segment grew 26% in 2025 — Q4 alone was up 47% year over year
Bambu's moat isn't just hardware: MakerWorld hit ~10 million monthly active users
For us: the price war is real, printers keep getting cheaper — and last week's Creality loss shows who's paying for it

topics.title: SUNLU FilaDC i10: A Dryer That Never Heats Your Filament
topics.description: Commercial-style desiccant drying, sized for ten spools

slides.heading: SUNLU FilaDC i10: Drying Without the Heat
slides.body: This is the commercial drying method finally sized for us: a 10-spool cabinet that circulates room-temperature air through molecular-sieve desiccant. The filament itself is NEVER heated — no more cooking your spools through endless dry cycles.
bullets: Air loops through the desiccant, which traps the moisture — filament stays at room temperature
When the sieve saturates, a PTC heater regenerates IT, not your filament, then flips back automatically
Ten 1 kg spools, humidity dialed anywhere from 10 to 55% RH
~0.23 kWh a day versus ~2.9 for a heated dryer, at 35 dB or quieter
Pre-orders open September 15 — price lands then, rumored under $200
Open question the launch photos don't answer: where the expelled moisture actually goes

topics.title: FibreSeeker 3: Continuous Carbon Fiber on a Desktop
topics.description: A $2,399 machine that lays unbroken fiber into your prints

slides.heading: FibreSeeker 3: Continuous Carbon Fiber Goes Desktop
slides.body: Not chopped-fiber filament — this machine lays UNBROKEN carbon fiber strands inside the print, the technique that lets plastic parts stand in for machined metal. After a $4.7M Kickstarter, FibreSeek opened a 500-unit global pre-sale on September 9.
bullets: Dual nozzle: 0.4 mm for regular FFF, 0.7 mm for fiber co-extrusion, with a built-in fiber cutter
Claimed 900 MPa tensile strength — the brochure math says 30× standard PLA
300 × 300 × 245 mm build volume, up to 500 mm/s in plain FFF mode, 65 °C heated chamber
US pre-sale opens September 15: $3,199 early bird against a $3,499 retail price — 500 units worldwide
Same rule as every pre-sale: that strength number is the vendor's — wait for independent tests

topics.title: Printabot Is Back: Printed Rails That Beat Steel
topics.description: PETG + PTFE linear rails outperform metal — suggested by our own Horizon-3D

slides.heading: Printabot: PETG + PTFE Rails vs. Steel — Printed Wins
slides.body: Our friend Printabot is back, and this one's a jaw-dropper: he replaced EVERY steel linear rail on a Sovol Zero CoreXY with printed PETG rails riding PTFE tube — and the printer ran BETTER than on its metal ball-bearing rails. Video's in Spanish; the results speak every language.

slides.heading: Why This One Matters
bullets: Printed rails means no bearing noise, no grease, pennies in material — and he measured print quality going UP
PTFE against smooth PETG is a naturally slick pair — no balls to pit, no preload to tune
Shout-out: our member Horizon-3D submitted this exact video on our GitHub — this is the topic pipeline working
Working on getting Printabot to join a meetup for a deep-dive — stay tuned

topics.title: INDX Update: Kits Are Shipping, Full Printers on Sale
topics.description: The toolchanger saga reaches actual customers

slides.heading: INDX: From Promise to Porch
slides.body: The toolchanger story we've tracked since spring finally reached the shipping stage: Prusa confirmed the first batch of INDX conversion kits is going out, and you can now order a complete CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX — assembled or kit, 4 or 8 tools.
bullets: First-batch conversion kits: shipping started, per Prusa's August 20 post
Complete INDX printers now orderable — no more converting an existing CORE One yourself
August 27: the bigger CORE One L+ got its INDX kits and assembled option too
Slicer catch still stands: PrusaSlicer 3.0's alpha ships WITHOUT INDX profiles — they arrive later through the Configuration Wizard
Rival watch: Sovol M1D preorders are live (last week), Co Print's Quadro Kickstarter is due in October — 2026 really is the toolchanger year

topics.title: Robotics Corner: Oomwoo, the Robot Vacuum You Print
topics.description: Open-source, offline-only, and built on your own printer

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: Print Your Own Robot Vacuum
slides.body: Maker's Pet launched Oomwoo — an open-source robot vacuum you 3D print and assemble yourself: printed chassis, Raspberry Pi brain, a cheap 2D LiDAR, ROS 2 underneath. And the design goal that makes it OUR kind of robot: it runs entirely offline. No cloud, no account, no microphone phoning home.
bullets: Everything is open — hardware, firmware, software, Apache 2.0, targeting ~$200 in parts
Runs ROS 2 with Nav2 and talks to Home Assistant — a real robotics stack, not a toy
The offline-only stance is a direct answer to the hijacked-vacuum horror stories — researchers took over camera-equipped Ecovacs units remotely
It's early: v0 covers the chassis, simulation, and LiDAR mapping; build instructions are due this fall
I've been in the project's GitHub discussions myself — jump in, this is a fun one to watch

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Salim's 3D-Printed PCB Motor
topics.description: An axial flux motor with the circuit board as its stator

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: A Motor Where the PCB IS the Stator
slides.body: This week's spotlight is Salim's Workshop and a build that rethinks what a motor even is: a rotary axial flux motor where the stator windings are traces on a printed circuit board, and the rotor is 3D printed around off-the-shelf magnets. Then he tested whether it actually works.

slides.heading: Why a Printed Motor Matters
bullets: Axial flux motors are prized for their flat, pancake form — and normally priced way out of hobby reach
The stator is just a PCB order and the rotor is just a print — two things every maker can already do
It runs: the video walks the full build and the real-world test, including what didn't work on the way
If motors become something we print and order like any other part, whole categories of builds open up — robots included

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Dry with desiccant, not heat cycles

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Stop Cooking Your Filament
slides.body: Tonight's Sunlu cabinet is built on a principle you can use for free, right now: moisture management beats repeated drying. Every heat-dry cycle ages your filament a little — the goal is to never need the oven in the first place.
bullets: Store spools in a sealed box or bag with desiccant and a $5 hygrometer — keep them dry instead of re-drying them
Recharge the DESICCANT in the oven, not the filament — silica gel comes back forever, polymer doesn't
Heat-dry a spool when it actually needs it (stringing, popping, matte surfaces), not on a schedule
September humidity is exactly when a $10 box of desiccant pays for itself
